extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing clear, engaging fiction prose (dialogue, description, openings) based on Elmore Leonard's ten rules and his master rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never open a book with weather.
rubrics_metrics.description: Never open a book with weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it's only to create atmosphere, and not a character's reaction to the weather, you don't want to go on too long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prologues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They can be annoying, especially if they precede a prologue, a foreword, and an introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never use a verb other than 'said' to carry dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.description: Never use a verb other than "said" to carry dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Said" is far less intrusive than grumbled, gasped, cautioned, lied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never use an adverb to modify the verb 'said.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Never use an adverb to modify the verb "said."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ("…he admonished gravely.") "To use an adverb this way (or almost any way) is a mortal sin."

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep your exclamation points under control.
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep your exclamation points under control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "You are allowed no more than two or three per 100,000 words of prose."

rubrics_metrics.name: Never use the words 'suddenly' or 'all hell broke loose.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Never use the words "suddenly" or "all hell broke loose."

rubrics_metrics.name: Use regional dialect, patois, sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phonetic spelling and apostrophe-heavy dialogue piles up fast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid detailed descriptions of characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hemingway showed how — let action and dialogue reveal character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't go into great detail describing places and things.
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't go into great detail describing places and things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description shouldn't bring the action to a standstill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try to leave out the part that readers tend to skip.
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to leave out the part that readers tend to skip.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Master Rule: 'If it sounds like writing, I rewrite it.'
rubrics_metrics.description: "If it sounds like writing, I rewrite it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Master rule summarizing the imperative to remove anything that reads as self-conscious or artificially 'written' rather than natural prose.
